identification.summary: Storm-2227 is a Microsoft temporary designation for a cluster of threat activity still in development. Microsoft's only located public mention lists it among multiple cybercriminal actors that used RedVDS infrastructure, a paid service renting unlicensed Windows RDP servers [S1]. Microsoft uses 'Storm-####' for newly discovered or unattributed clusters that have not yet met the criteria for a named actor [S2].
identification.notes: Microsoft name: Storm-2227 (group in development). The RedVDS report names it alongside Storm-0259, Storm-1575 and Storm-1747; the RedVDS operator itself is tracked separately as Storm-2470 [S1]. Do not merge these clusters. The report gives no further detail on Storm-2227, so the RedVDS context is customer-of-infrastructure only and does not describe its objectives or tradecraft [S1].

targeting.notes: RedVDS-enabled activity as a whole targeted legal, construction, manufacturing, real estate, healthcare and education organizations in the US, Canada, UK, France, Germany and Australia [S1]. The report does not state which of these victims were Storm-2227's, so none are attributed to it.

campaigns.name: Use of RedVDS infrastructure (Microsoft DCU disruption report)
campaigns.summary: Microsoft's 14 January 2026 report lists Storm-2227 among multiple cybercriminal actors that leveraged RedVDS, a virtual dedicated server provider used for business email compromise, mass phishing, account takeover and financial fraud. Microsoft's Digital Crimes Unit and law enforcement facilitated a disruption of RedVDS infrastructure. No Storm-2227-specific activity is described [S1].

diamond.infrastructure: RedVDS rented Windows RDP servers (operator tracked by Microsoft as Storm-2470) were used by multiple actors including Storm-2227 [S1].

gaps: Fact-check search confirmed the RedVDS report (14 Jan 2026) and Storm-2470 as operator, but did not surface the Storm-2227 mention itself; that listing is not independently re-verified [S1].

No Microsoft blog, Threat Analytics entry or third-party report describing Storm-2227's own TTPs, targets, objectives or timeline was found in searches; only one passing mention in the RedVDS report [S1].
Motivation is not stated for Storm-2227; the report describes RedVDS users as cybercriminal and financially motivated in general, not this cluster specifically [S1].
Not established whether Storm-2227 is state-linked or criminal beyond the 'cybercriminal actors' grouping in [S1].
The Storm-#### definition is taken from Microsoft's threat actor naming page and search-result text [S2].
The Microsoft threat-actor mapping file lists no aliases or other vendor names for this cluster.

sources.title: Inside RedVDS: How a single virtual desktop provider fueled worldwide cybercriminal operations
